name: uk.co.getmovely/getmovely
title: GetMovely
description: Search homes for sale and off-market, sold prices, EPC, stamp duty: 25m homes in England and Wales.

tools.name: search_addresses
tools.description:
Find homes in England and Wales by street, postcode, town or address. Each row has
the home's last sale, freehold or leasehold, whether it is owner-occupied, whether it
is listed for sale, and its response likelihood (High = listed for sale and
owner-occupied, Medium = owner-occupied, Unknown = no record). Filter with
`response_likelihood` to answer "which homes on this street are owner-occupied and for
sale", or sort by it. Returns 20 per page (`limit`, up to 60), newest sale first by default.
If the street name exists in several places the answer lists the places as `streets`
instead of rows; a search with the town or postcode added returns the homes.
When nothing matches exactly the answer says so (`exact_match` false) and gives at most
ten of the nearest names, which may be in other towns: Scotland and Northern Ireland are
not covered.

query.description: Street, postcode, outcode, town or full address, as a person would type it: 'Merton Road, SW19', 'BS7 8', 'Ash Street, Salford M6', '41 Denning Road NW3'.
query.title: Query

sale_pairs.description: Filter to homes whose sale history contains these sales, each as 'price:year', e.g. ['450000:2019']. This is how to find the exact address behind a listing or an advert that shows past sales.
sale_pairs.title: Sale Pairs

response_likelihood.description: Only homes with this response likelihood. 'High' = listed for sale and owner-occupied (the homes where a letter reaches an owner who is selling). 'Medium' = owner-occupied, not listed for sale. 'Unknown' = no public record that the owner lives there. 'Owner on GetMovely' = the owner has claimed the address. Leave out for all homes.
response_likelihood.title: Response Likelihood

sort.description: 'recent' newest sale first (default); 'likelihood' High first, then Medium, then the rest; 'price_desc' / 'price_asc' by last sale price; 'addr' by address.
sort.title: Sort

limit.description: Addresses per page: 20 by default, up to 60. Ask for fewer when one home is wanted.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: get_address
tools.description:
One home's card, the quick answer to "is this house for sale" and "does the owner
live there": full address, last sale, freehold or leasehold, whether it is
owner-occupied (from its Energy Performance Certificate), whether it is listed for sale
(with the portal, the agent and the link to the advert), its response likelihood (High
= listed for sale and owner-occupied), and the link that opens a letter to its owner
on GetMovely.

Use it for those yes/no facts about a home you already have an `akey` for (from
search_addresses or any row another tool returned). For prices, energy, the street and
the area use address_report (everything) or the single-topic tools. An `akey` comes
only from another tool's answer; an unknown one fails with "address not found". A field that is null means no
public record, not "no": `owner_occupied` null is not the same as false.

tools.name: address_report
tools.description:
Everything GetMovely knows about one home in one call. `home` gives the facts in
brief: freehold or leasehold, whether it is owner-occupied (from its Energy
Performance Certificate), whether it is listed for sale, and its response likelihood
(High = listed for sale and owner-occupied). `tiles` is the nine-part report the
website shows: sold-price
history, building type and size, energy rating with costs and improvements, local
market (price per m2 nearby), area price trend, market history (asking price, time on
the market, the agent and the link to the advert when it is for sale), nearby
essentials, recorded crime and air quality. `contact_owner_url` opens a letter to its
owner. About 15 KB: use get_address, sale_history, energy_performance or price_check
when one part is enough. Limited to 60 reports per hour per caller, a limit
sale_history, energy_performance, price_check and compare_homes share.

tools.name: street_price_per_m2
tools.description:
Recent Land Registry sales near one home with their EPC floor area, as pounds per
square metre and per square foot by year. Scope is the home's own postcode when it has
enough sized sales, otherwise the whole street; `scope` says which. Market-value
(category A) sales only.

Use it for "what do homes on this street go for per square metre". To judge one
price or an asking price use price_check, which sets the street beside the district;
for a list of the sales themselves use recent_sales with the street as `area`; for a
whole district use area_overview. Takes an `akey` from search_addresses or any row
another tool returned. A street with no sale that has a floor area on record returns
an empty `years`; that means too little evidence, not a price of zero.

tools.name: price_trends
tools.description:
What freehold or leasehold, new build or resale, energy rating and floor area are
worth per square metre in one postcode district, for one property type (D detached,
S semi-detached, T terraced, F flat), by whole calendar year, against the national
picture. Property type is always held constant because it is the confounder that
makes the naive comparison lie. Every figure is a median of at least a minimum
number of sales; no per-address data. For a plain summary of a district across all
its property types use area_overview.

Use it for "is a leasehold flat cheaper here", "what is an A-rated house worth over a
D", "do bigger homes cost less per m2". For several districts use compare_areas; for
one home use price_check. When a district has too few sales of that type the tool
fails and names the property types it does have, so ask again with one of those.

outcode.description: Postcode district (outcode) such as 'SW19', 'BS7', 'M6'. A full postcode is accepted; only the district is used.
outcode.title: Outcode

tools.name: whats_nearby
tools.description:
Train, tram and ferry stops, bus stops, primary and secondary schools, cafes and
restaurants, pubs, takeaways, supermarkets, parks and play areas around a home, from
official open data, within 100 m to 2 km: for each kind the count, the nearest one and
its distance. Pass `closest` with a kind to get the nearest N of that kind instead,
however far (the way to ask "how far is the station" for a rural home). To compare
many homes, pass up to 50 keys in `akeys` and get one row per home in `homes`: one
call covers the whole list.

Use it for amenities and transport. Crime and air quality are in address_report;
compare_homes also names the nearest station, school, supermarket and park for two to
four homes. Keys come from search_addresses or any row another tool returned. A kind
with nothing inside the radius is left out of `kinds` (an empty `kinds` means nothing
within it at all): widen `radius_m` or use `closest`. Schools here are by distance only, not catchment
or Ofsted rating.

akey.description: Address key of one home, from search_addresses. Give this or `akeys`.
akey.title: Akey

closest.description: Instead of counts within the radius, list the N closest places of this one kind (expanding rings up to 16 km).
closest.title: Closest

n.description: How many closest places, with `closest`: 10 by default, up to 25 for one home; at most 3 per home with `akeys`.
n.title: N

akeys.description: Several homes in one call, up to 50 address keys: use this instead of calling once per home, for example for every home recent_sales or search_homes_for_sale returned.
akeys.title: Akeys

tools.name: tenure_check
tools.description:
Whether homes matching an address are freehold or leasehold, from the tenure recorded
on the latest Land Registry sale of each exact address, with that sale's date. Up to 12
candidates; null tenure means no recorded sale with a tenure. Matching is by text: when
`fuzzy` is true or the rows are not the address asked for, use search_addresses, whose
rows carry `tenure_at_last_sale` for the exact home.

query.description: Address or street with postcode, e.g. '12 Church Lane, BS7 8AB'.
query.title: Query

tools.name: house_age
tools.description:
The construction age band of homes matching an address, from the Energy Performance
Certificate, with what that era means for the construction, plus the first recorded sale
year as corroboration and the property type. Up to 12 candidates.

Use it for "when was this house built" and "what is it built like" (solid walls, cavity
walls, asbestos era). It takes the address as text, so no `akey` is needed; for the
full energy picture of one home use energy_performance. Matching is by text: when
`fuzzy` is true the rows are near matches, not the address asked for, and
search_addresses finds the exact home. `band` null means that home has no certificate
with an age band; `first_yr` is the first sale since 1995, not the build year.

tools.name: sale_history
tools.description:
Every recorded sale of one home since 1995, from HM Land Registry price paid
data: price, month and year, the price per square metre each sale works out at on
the home's current EPC floor area, and the change from the first sale to the last.
The short answer to "what did this house sell for"; address_report has the rest.

tools.name: energy_performance
tools.description:
A home's Energy Performance Certificate in plain terms: rating and score now and
the rating it could reach, modelled running costs a year for heating, hot water and
lighting, carbon dioxide, which parts of the building are weak (walls, roof,
windows), and the assessor's own list of improvements with their indicative costs.
Costs are the assessor's model at the prices of the certificate's date, not bills.

Use it for "how efficient is this home", "what would it cost to heat" and "what
should I upgrade", when an `akey` is known (from search_addresses or any row another
tool returned). address_report carries the same certificate among its nine parts;
house_age gives only the build era. A home with no certificate returns
`certificate: false` and a `reason` (one not sold or let since 2008 may never have
had one); that is missing evidence, not a bad rating. Check `certificate_year`:
an old certificate may predate later work on the home.

tools.name: price_check
tools.description:
Is a price in line? Works out the price per square metre from the home's EPC
floor area and sets it against three things: what homes of the same type sold for
per square metre in the same postcode district in the latest whole year, with the
quartiles; recent sales on the home's own street or postcode; and the home's own
last sale moved by the district's change since. Also gives the price range the
district's quartiles imply for this floor area. Arithmetic on public medians, not a
valuation, and the answer carries the caveats to pass on. Shares the address
report's limit of 60 an hour per caller.

Use it for "is this price fair" or "what might this home be worth" on one home with
an `akey` (from search_addresses or any row another tool returned). For a home on
the market, negotiation_brief adds the asking-price cuts and time on the market.
When the home has no floor area on record, or its district too few sales of its
type, the answer has `comparable: false` and a `reason` naming the tool to use
instead, and no figure is given.

price_gbp.description: The price to check, in pounds: an asking price, an offer, a valuation. Leave out to get what the district's prices imply for a home this size (and, when the home is advertised for sale, to check its asking price).
price_gbp.title: Price Gbp

tools.name: negotiation_brief
tools.description:
The evidence a buyer brings to an offer on one home that is advertised for
sale: the asking price now, every change to it GetMovely has seen on the advert
(with dates and the total cut), how long it has been on the market, the asking
price per square metre against what the same type of home sold for in the postcode
district, against recent sales on the street, and against the home's own last sale
moved by the district's change since, then the points that follow, in plain
sentences. Evidence, not a valuation or advice on what to offer. For a home that
is not on the market use price_check. Shares the address report's limit of 60 an
hour per caller.

tools.name: buyer_checks
tools.description:
The things a buyer should look into before offering on one home, in one call:
flood risk from rivers and the sea and from surface water (Environment Agency
bands); planning protections (conservation area, listed building entries at or
next to it, article 4 direction, green belt, national park, National Landscape,
World Heritage Site, scheduled monument); the nearest primary and secondary
schools with their last published Ofsted grade and their latest Department for
Education results; broadband availability in the postcode and mobile coverage in
the council; the neighbourhood's deprivation rank and Census 2021 profile; council
tax by band and metered energy use; private rents in the council; recorded crime
and air quality; the weak parts of the building and the upgrades its Energy
Performance Certificate lists; and freehold or leasehold, then the questions those
facts raise.

Use it for "is there anything I should worry about with this house", "does it
flood", "is it listed or in a conservation area", "what are the schools like near
it", "what is the broadband like". Takes an `akey` from search_addresses or any row
another tool returned. `flags` lists only what stood out; an empty list means
nothing in this open data did, not that the home has been surveyed or searched.
Flood bands and the neighbourhood describe the area, not the building; a listed
building entry is a point, so "at or next to" means check the record; conservation
areas and article 4 directions are only as complete as each council has published
them. Shares the address report's limit of 60 an hour.

tools.name: compare_homes
tools.description:
Two to four homes side by side, one row each: type and floor area, tenure, last
sale and its price per square metre, energy rating and modelled running cost, what
the street has sold for recently, the district trend, whether it is
owner-occupied, whether it is listed for sale and its response likelihood (High =
both), the nearest supermarket, primary school, station and park, recorded crime
and air quality. Each row links its own report and the page
that opens a letter to its owner. Counts as one address report per home against the
60 an hour limit.

akeys.description: Two to four address keys from search_addresses.
akeys.title: Akeys

tools.name: find_address_from_sale_history
tools.description:
Property portals often hide the house number but show the home's past sale
prices. HM Land Registry records every sale by exact address, so the sale history
identifies the home: give the area and the sales, get the address or addresses that
match. One match is the answer. Several means add another sale or a tighter area.
None means check the year (portals show the year the sale completed) or widen the
area. The returned `akey` works with every per-address tool.

area.description: Where the listing says the home is: a street with its district ('Merton Road, SW19'), a postcode or its first half ('SW19 1'), or a town.
area.title: Area

sales.description: Past sales shown on the listing, each as 'price:year' in pounds, for example ['450000:2019', '310000:2012']. More sales narrow it faster.
sales.title: Sales

match.description: 'any' (default): the home has these sales, possibly among others. 'last': the newest sale given is the home's most recent sale. 'only': the home has exactly these sales and no others.
match.title: Match

tools.name: area_overview
tools.description:
What homes sell for in one postcode district, for every property type sold
there (detached, semi-detached, terraced, flats): the latest whole year's median
price per square metre with its quartiles and number of sales, the change since
the series began in 2015, and the year in progress against the same months a year
earlier. `market_now` is the district this month: Rightmove adverts on the market,
new in 28 days, the share whose latest change was a price cut, days on the market
and days until adverts came down (an accepted offer or a withdrawal), by type,
with England and Wales alongside; homes getting an energy certificate for a sale
(the earliest public sign of supply) against a year earlier; and the share of
sales arranged without open marketing. Given a region, council or town instead,
it answers for the whole place: per property type the typical price per square
metre across its districts, sales, cheapest and dearest district and the change
on a year, with its districts side by side. Use compare_areas to set districts
against each other and price_trends for what tenure, energy rating or size are
worth within one.

outcode.description: Postcode district such as 'SW19', 'BS7', 'M6' (a full postcode is accepted; only the district is used), or a bigger place: a region ('London', 'North West'), a council ('Camden', 'Manchester', 'Cornwall') or a town.
outcode.title: Outcode

tools.name: compare_areas
tools.description:
Two to six postcode districts side by side for one property type: latest whole
year's median price per square metre with quartiles and sales, change since 2015,
the year in progress against the same months a year earlier and, when a floor area
is given, what that many square metres cost at each district's median; then
`market_now` for each: adverts of that type on the market, the share whose latest
change was a price cut, median days on the market and until adverts came down,
and sale certificates against a year earlier. Property type is held constant
because comparing a district of flats with a district of houses compares the mix,
not the place.

outcodes.description: Two to six postcode districts, for example ['SW19', 'BS7', 'M20'].
outcodes.title: Outcodes

property_type.description: One type, held constant across the districts: D detached, S semi-detached, T terraced, F flat.
property_type.title: Property Type

floor_area_m2.description: Optional floor area to price at each district's median, for example 100.
floor_area_m2.title: Floor Area M2

tools.name: district_statistics
tools.description:
GetMovely's published research for one local authority district, with England
and Wales alongside: the share of homes that are leasehold (houses and flats
separately), how many years pass between sales of the same home and the share not
sold for 20 years or more, the share of purchases resold within two years, how
big homes are (median floor area, by property type and built form), and the
council's band D council tax with its private rents and a gross rental yield by
property type. Districts are
named as HM Land Registry and the EPC register name them; an unclear name returns
the candidates. For prices use area_overview, which works by postcode district.

district.description: A local authority district in England or Wales by name: 'Bristol', 'Camden', 'Merton', 'Leeds', 'Cardiff'. 'London' gives Greater London as a whole and 'England and Wales' the national figures.
district.title: District

tools.name: search_homes_for_sale
tools.description:
Homes currently advertised for sale in an area of England or Wales, by criteria:
"find me a 3-bed under £400k in BS7", "flats over 60 m2 in Wimbledon". Filter by
asking price, bedrooms, property type and floor area; and, for adverts GetMovely has
matched to an exact address, by freehold or leasehold, energy rating and whether the
owner lives there. Each row has the asking price, bedrooms, type, floor area, price
per square metre, when it was listed and days on the market, the portal, agent and
link to the advert, and for a matched home its address key, response likelihood and
the link that opens a letter to its owner. 20 a page; `total` is every advert that
fits. Adverts are re-read regularly, so a brand-new listing can be missing.

area.description: Where to look: a postcode district ('BS7'), a full postcode ('SW19 1AB'), a town ('Wimbledon'), or a street with its district or town ('Elm Road, BS7').
area.title: Area

property_type.description: From the advert's own words. 'house' is any house including bungalows; 'flat' includes apartments and maisonettes; 'terraced' includes end of terrace.
property_type.title: Property Type

min_floor_area_m2.description: Smallest floor area in square metres. Adverts with no floor area on record are left out.
min_floor_area_m2.title: Min Floor Area M2

tenure.description: As recorded at the home's last sale. Only adverts matched to an exact address can be filtered this way.
tenure.title: Tenure

epc_ratings.description: Energy ratings to keep, for example ['A','B','C']. Only adverts matched to an exact address.
epc_ratings.title: Epc Ratings

owner_occupied.description: True: only homes whose Energy Performance Certificate records them as owner-occupied (response likelihood High). Only adverts matched to an exact address.
owner_occupied.title: Owner Occupied

sort.description: 'newest' advert first (default), by asking price, by asking price per square metre (lowest first), or largest first.
sort.title: Sort

tools.name: describe_homes_for_sale
tools.description:
Find homes for sale from a description in the person's own words ("riverside flat
in London", "bungalow with a south-facing garden near Totnes"), or from tags the
adverts themselves state (chain free, probate, needs modernisation, waterside...),
or both. Ranks the adverts GetMovely has read by how well their own text matches;
search_homes_for_sale is the structured version of this search (exact bedroom
counts, tenure, energy rating, owner-occupied). Give `description` or `signals` or
both. Each row has the asking price, type, floor area where known, the advert link,
its tags, how well it matched, and for an advert tied to an exact address the
`akey` every per-address tool takes. An empty answer means nothing matched the
description well, not that nothing is for sale; `unread` counts homes that fit the
filters whose adverts GetMovely has not read in full, which a description cannot
reach. 30 a page.

description.description: The home in the person's own words, for example 'riverside flat with a balcony' or 'quirky cottage that needs work'. Leave the area out of it and pass `area` instead; price, bedrooms and size written here are lifted into filters.
description.title: Description

area.description: A postcode district ('SW19') or a place name ('London', 'Bath'). Unlike search_homes_for_sale, a whole city works here.
area.title: Area

signals.description: Tags derived from each advert's own text; a tagged listing is one whose advert says it. Combine with or use instead of `description`.
signals.title: Signals

sort.description: 'best' (default) is match order for a description and newest for tags alone.
sort.title: Sort

tools.name: find_homes_not_for_sale
tools.description:
Homes that are NOT advertised for sale, by criteria: the homes a buyer could write
to. "Which houses on this street could I write to", "owner-occupied houses over
120 m2 in BS7 that last sold before 2005". Filter by property type, floor area,
freehold or leasehold, energy rating, when and for how much the home last sold, and
whether the owner lives there. Each row has the address, type, floor area, energy
rating, last sale and its price per square metre, whether it is owner-occupied, its
response likelihood, and `contact_owner_url`, the link that opens a letter to that
home's owner on GetMovely. 20 a page.

area.description: Where to look: a postcode district ('BS7'), a full postcode ('SW19 1AB'), a town ('Wimbledon'), or a street with its district or town ('Elm Road, BS7'). A town of more than four postcode districts must be narrowed to a district.
area.title: Area

property_type.description: From the home's Energy Performance Certificate, which does not say detached, semi-detached or terraced.
property_type.title: Property Type

tenure.description: As recorded at the home's last sale, so homes with no recorded sale are left out.
tenure.title: Tenure

epc_ratings.description: Energy ratings to keep, for example ['E','F','G'] for homes that need work.
epc_ratings.title: Epc Ratings

last_sold_before_year.description: Last sold before this year: long-held homes. Homes with no recorded sale since 1995 are included too unless no_recorded_sale says otherwise.
last_sold_before_year.title: Last Sold Before Year

last_sold_after_year.description: Last sold in or after this year.
last_sold_after_year.title: Last Sold After Year

no_recorded_sale.description: Homes with no sale on record since 1995 (held longest of all): 'only' those, or 'exclude' them.
no_recorded_sale.title: No Recorded Sale

owner_occupied.description: True: only homes whose Energy Performance Certificate records them as owner-occupied (response likelihood Medium), where a letter reaches the owner.
owner_occupied.title: Owner Occupied

sort.description: 'owner_occupied_first' (default, the website's order), 'longest_held' oldest last sale first, 'recent' newest sale first, by last sale price, or largest floor area first.
sort.title: Sort

tools.name: recent_sales
tools.description:
What sold in an area, newest first: "what sold near here this year", "flats sold in
SW19 since January for under £500k". HM Land Registry price paid data for a postcode
district, postcode, street or small town, filtered by property type, date range,
price range, floor area, tenure and new build. Each sale has the address, price,
date, type, freehold or leasehold, and the price per square metre where the home has
a floor area on its Energy Performance Certificate. Market-value sales only. Sales
reach the register two weeks to two months after completion, so the last few weeks
are always incomplete. For one home's own history use sale_history.

area.description: Where to look: a postcode district ('BS7'), a full postcode ('SW19 1AB'), a town ('Wimbledon'), or a street with its district or town ('Elm Road, BS7'). A town of more than six postcode districts must be narrowed to a district.
area.title: Area

property_type.description: D detached, S semi-detached, T terraced, F flat (the Land Registry's own classes).
property_type.title: Property Type

sold_from.description: Earliest sale date, 'YYYY-MM-DD', or a year ('2026' means from 1 January 2026).
sold_from.title: Sold From

sold_to.description: Latest sale date, 'YYYY-MM-DD', or a year ('2025' means to 31 December 2025).
sold_to.title: Sold To

min_floor_area_m2.description: Only sales of homes at least this big. Needs a floor area on an Energy Performance Certificate; with this filter the total is not counted.
min_floor_area_m2.title: Min Floor Area M2

new_build.description: New-build sales only, or leave them out.
new_build.title: New Build

tools.name: stamp_duty
tools.description:
How much stamp duty: Stamp Duty Land Tax for a home in England, Land Transaction Tax
for one in Wales, for a home mover, a first-time buyer or an additional property,
with the tax in each band and the other two buyer cases beside it. Uses the
residential rates published on GOV.UK and gov.wales, quoted in `sources` with the
date they were read. An estimate for a standard purchase of one freehold or
existing leasehold home by individuals: shared ownership, new leases with rent,
companies, mixed-use property and linked purchases follow other rules, and the
official calculator is linked in the answer.

country.description: Where the home is. England uses Stamp Duty Land Tax; Wales uses Land Transaction Tax.
country.title: Country

buyer.description: 'home_mover': replacing a main home, the standard rates. 'first_time': every buyer is a first-time buyer. 'additional': the buyer will own more than one home after the purchase (second home, buy to let).
buyer.title: Buyer

non_uk_resident.description: Buyer is not a UK resident (adds 2% in England).
non_uk_resident.title: Non Uk Resident

tools.name: draft_letter
tools.description:
Hand a letter the person has agreed with you to GetMovely. Returns `letter_url`: a
link that opens the letter composer for that home on getmovely.co.uk with the text
already filled in, where the person reads it, can edit it, and sends it themselves
(free; sending needs a free account, and GetMovely prints and posts it). Nothing is
sent and nothing is stored by this call: the text travels inside the link. Checks
the website's letter rules first (200 words, 1,400 characters) and says what to fix
if the text breaks them. The text is the person's own; the guide
'letter-to-homeowner-asking-to-buy-house' says what a good letter contains.

letter_text.description: The message the person has agreed, as plain text: what goes in the body of the letter. No address block, date or sign-off name is needed; GetMovely lays the letter out.
letter_text.title: Letter Text

tools.name: search_guides
tools.description:
GetMovely's plain-English guides to buying and selling homes in England and
Wales: contacting an owner directly and the law on it, buying or selling without an
estate agent, finding who owns a property or the address behind a listing, how
often sales fall through, speeding a sale up, best and final offers, stopping
unwanted letters. Returns the closest guides with a one-paragraph summary and the
questions each answers; read_guide gives the full text with its sources.

query.description: What the person wants to know, in plain words: 'is it legal to write to a homeowner', 'who owns the freehold', 'how many house sales fall through'. Leave out to list every guide.
query.title: Query

tools.name: read_guide
tools.description:
The full text of one GetMovely guide as Markdown, with the questions it
answers, the primary sources it cites (GOV.UK, HM Land Registry, the ICO, The
Property Ombudsman and others) and the date it was last updated. General
information, not legal advice. Each guide carries its `url`.

slug.description: Guide slug from search_guides, for example 'is-it-legal-to-write-to-a-homeowner'.
slug.title: Slug
